result.markdown: --- title: "10 · Generalized linear models (GLM)" subtitle: "Week 3" --- ::: {.guiding-q} What to do if the DV is not normal? ::: [The first assumption we relax: **normality**.]{.accent} ## In this session - Responses that are counts, proportions or binary choices - The three parts of a GLM: distribution, linear predictor, link function - Poisson and binomial models; offsets for observation time - Overdispersion and the negative binomial model - Interpreting coefficients and plotting predictions on the response scale ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [Link function](../../glossary.qmd#link-function), [Log-odds (logit)](../../glossary.qmd#log-odds), [Offset](../../glossary.qmd#offset), [Overdispersion](../../glossary.qmd#overdispersion), [Zero-inflation](../../glossary.qmd#zero-inflation), [Complete separation](../../glossary.qmd#complete-separation) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - choose a distribution and link function that fit the response, - fit Poisson and binomial GLMs and interpret them on the response scale, - detect and handle overdispersion. ## Simulate first Counts of approaches per focal observation, increasing with age on the log scale. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(10) age <- runif(150, 0, 12) # months mu <- exp(0.2 + 0.12 * age) # log link counts <- rpois(150, mu) m <- glm(counts ~ age, family = poisson) round(coef(m), 2) # back on the log scale ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> (Intercept) age #> 0.33 0.11 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} round(exp(coef(m)[2]), 2) # multiplicative change per month ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> age #> 1.11 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot(age, counts, pch = 19, col = adjustcolor("#1b6f8a", .5), xlab = "Age (months)", ylab = "Count") curve(predict(m, data.frame(age = x), type = "response"), add = TRUE, col = "#c0392b", lwd = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](10-glm_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=975} ::: ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - Gelman, Hill & Vehtari (2020), ch. 13–15. - Fox (2016), ch. 14–15.
